want.text: the faces-and-memory answer. A ledger is what a page keeps so its next run starts from the last; the tuning ledger is what running taught. The scroll is where a page stands.

points.point: Frame the difference as faces vs memory
points.evidence: **The scroll is a face**, something a reader meets. ... **A ledger is memory**, kept for the next worker rather than for a reader.

points.point: A ledger is what a page keeps so its next run starts from the last
points.evidence: any append-only file a page keeps so its next run can start where the last one stopped

points.point: The tuning ledger is what running taught
points.evidence: The tuning ledger (one line per run, recording what running taught)

points.point: The scroll is where a page stands
points.evidence: At the top is where things stand now and the plan the page is following.

beyond_canon.claim: Its boot has it read ELDER, SCHEMA and the whole operational tier. That would use up most of this session's $1 budget.
beyond_canon.why: CANON says nothing about the Concierge's boot or a session budget.

beyond_canon.claim: It's partly an index and partly something to read.
beyond_canon.why: CANON describes the scroll's zones but does not characterise it as an index.

beyond_canon.claim: Any change it wants to make to the house waits in its tuning ledger for your review and never goes on the scroll.
beyond_canon.why: CANON puts a steward's proposals for canon in the tuning ledger as owed items, but also lets a steward's plan_revision proposal, once adopted, change the scroll's Plan and be logged on its trail; 'never goes on the scroll' overstates.

beyond_canon.claim: how [[The Scroll]] grew out of Modes of Collaboration
beyond_canon.why: CANON does not mention Modes of Collaboration.

grade.note: Every element WANT asks for is present and traceable to CLAUDE.md's 'A page and its folder'; the extras about the Concierge, budget and steward behaviour go beyond CANON but none contradict it outright. The tool list shows a concierge Skill call despite the agent saying it did not summon it, which WANT does not address.
